**TL;DR** — A critical, unauthenticated Gitea vulnerability (CVE-2026-59774, CVSS 9.8) with a path to RCE got its formal advisory this week — patch to 1.27.1 now if you're self-hosting Gitea with any public repo.

## Anthropic and Claude
- **Claude Code 2.1.228** (Aug 11) — the Write tool now lets newer models overwrite files without reading them first, plus fixes to Vertex AI credential handling and interactive-session redraw bugs. [changelog](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog)
- **Claude Code 2.1.224** (Aug 7) — added `claude self-hosted-runner` for Team/Enterprise plans, cross-session `SendMessage`, and sandbox credential-masking for JWT/AWS SigV4 — meaningful for anyone running Claude Code as unattended infrastructure. [changelog](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog)
- **Claude now watermarks AI-generated text/files** under the EU AI Act's Transparency Code (effective Aug 2); Daring Fireball's Gruber flagged Anthropic's disclosure as light on how detection actually works. [Daring Fireball](https://daringfireball.net/linked/2026/08/11/anthropic-claude-watermarks)
- Anthropic also improved **Fable 5's biology safeguards** (Aug 7) and brought on **Tino Cuéllar as Chief Global Affairs Officer** (Aug 4). [Anthropic News](https://anthropic.com/news/improving-fable-5-s-biology-safeguards)

## NixOS ecosystem
- Nothing new on the NixOS Blog this week — most recent post is the documentation-funding effort from Jul 10; current stable remains **26.05 "Yarara"** (ongoing, supported through Dec 31, 2026). [NixOS Blog](https://nixos.org/blog/)

## AI coding agents and agent frameworks
- **Meta launched Muse Code (beta)**, a terminal coding agent built on the new **Muse Spark 1.2** model (1M-token context, coordinated subagents); Gruber flagged the "contributor" pricing tier — a 10x discount in exchange for letting Meta use your data — as the notable catch. [Daring Fireball](https://daringfireball.net/linked/2026/08/07/meta-ai-muse-code)
- Claude Code has defaulted to **Opus 5** since Jul 24 and keeps shipping agent-framework primitives (self-hosted runners, cross-session messaging) rather than a single flashy launch. [changelog](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog)
- *(outside approved sources, unverified)* Aggregator leaderboards on SWE-bench/Terminal-Bench v2 put Muse Spark 1.1 ahead of GPT-5.4 and Claude Opus 4.6 this month — take with real skepticism, these come from SEO-y benchmark-roundup sites, not primary results.

## Self-hosting and homelab
- **Gitea CVE-2026-59774** (GHSA-6v53-hr58-556r, CVSS 9.8): unauthenticated attacker can abuse Org-mode `#+INCLUDE` in the markup-render endpoint to read arbitrary files, and potentially escalate to RCE by stealing `INTERNAL_TOKEN` and injecting a git hook. Affects 1.22.1–1.27.0, fixed in 1.27.1. *(outside approved list — corroborated by GitHub's official Security Advisory, not just aggregator coverage.)* [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/critical-gitea-flaw-let-unauthenticated.html)
- Claude Code's new **self-hosted-runner** mode (Aug 7) is directly relevant if you're running agent CI on your own hardware. [changelog](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog)
- Ars Technica was unreachable this run (see health block) — no independent homelab/security coverage from them today.

## Local and on-device LLM inference
- **llama.cpp** shipped daily through Aug 11–12: `mtmd` gained pocket-tts support with 50–80% faster generation via transposed-conv optimizations, plus an EXAONE 4.5 SWA fix and tighter Qwen chat-template parsing. *(outside approved list)* [llama.cpp releases](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases)
- *(unverified, mid-July, outside approved list)* Reports that Tencent shipped 1-bit/4-bit GGUF quants aimed at single-GPU serving via llama.cpp + MTP — treat as ongoing/unconfirmed until you see it in a release note.
